bugs.rootCause: The V3 Pattern-A task 01KY5205H4A338M8NGGFHNPR1J dispatched correctly and the agent is genuinely in-flight (headless `claude --resume` alive, active rustc compiling ainb inside the worktree, in-progress uncommitted edits to docs/hangar/README.md + tui-keybindings.md + new troubleshooting.md). It reached no terminal state only because the driving/poll gave up too early: the subagent turn was force-ended ~5 min after dispatch (poll-log stops at iter=9 / 15:04:45) while the agent was still doing legitimate long work. This is not a hangar bug: fail-closed correctly refused to mark it done, but the classification-as-failure is a timing artifact. Proof the window was simply too short: run_history row 01KY4CKGNZ... (a prior identical docs task) ran 1784705977976->1784706351807 = 373807 ms (~6.2 min) and finished status='success' — longer than the ~5 min this cycle waited before force-ending.
bugs.fixPlan: For the NEXT cycle's driving only (no code change): after dispatch, let v3final-poll.sh run to its full 30-minute budget in the background (or use a Monitor until-loop on `select status from agent_task_queue`) and classify the task ONLY on a genuine terminal state (done/failed) or a real timeout — do not end the driving turn at ~5 min. Then apply the artifact checks (>=1 commit whose diff touches docs, transcript completion). Budget >= ~10-12 min minimum given prior runs land at ~6+ min with a cold build.

bugs.rootCause: The contributing reason the task overran the window: the Pattern-A brief (issue.description) for a docs-drift task instructs the agent to 'verify every drift item against the actual code and CLI behavior' and 'regenerate the CLI reference wherever the freshness check requires it'. 'Regenerate the CLI reference' maps to the real scripts/gen-cli-reference.sh, which runs `cargo run` on the ainb binary. In a fresh worktree with a cold target/ dir, that forces a full multi-minute workspace compile (observed: rustc at 249% CPU building ainb-core inside the worktree) which dominates task time and is why a docs-only task blows past a short verify window.
bugs.fixPlan: Pattern-B refinement run for the drift-fix brief so it fits any reasonable window: pick one of (a) drop the 'regenerate the CLI reference' clause from the drift-fix task and split CLI-ref regeneration into its own task, making the drift fix pure doc-editing; or (b) pre-warm/share a built target/ into the worktree before dispatch so the cargo build is warm; or (c) explicitly scope the brief to editing the doc files without requiring a compile. Preferred: (a) — keeps the docs-drift task doc-only and deterministic.
